comment: The revert-check of `domain-vocabulary`'s fourteen refusals (change `domain-vocabulary-is-declared`, task 7.1): one mutation per refusal word, each removing the guard that raises it and naming the case that must fail when it is gone. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/tests/check-glossary-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how, `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule. `case-cmd` runs one named case (`--case {case}`), so a mutation pays one case and not the suite. Every search is one line, unique in `tools/check-glossary.sh`, because the runner's replacement is literal and line-based; the file is restored byte for byte afterwards.

mutations.label: phantom
mutations.search: emit 1 phantom "$key" "$where" "the declared $role surface '$name' is observed nowhere in the census"
mutations.why: a declared surface the census never observes is refused, so a word the code does not carry cannot be declared into existence

mutations.label: drift
mutations.search: emit 1 drift "$key" "$dline" "declared=$name observed=$form in the $role role, which the row forbids"
mutations.why: a forbidden form observed in the role it is forbidden in is a finding naming the file and the line, so a rename cannot leave the old spelling behind unremarked

mutations.label: undecided
mutations.search: emit 1 undecided "$key" "$where" "the token is observed as $topform $topcount and $(printf '%s' "$second" | cut -f3) $(printf '%s' "$second" | cut -f4) in the $role role, and the row declares no canonical form"
mutations.why: a spelling the code splits evenly is refused until a canonical form is declared, because no majority can settle it

mutations.label: overruled
mutations.search: emit 1 overruled "$key" "$where" "declared=$canonical($ccount) observed=$topform($topcount), a majority the declaration contradicts"
mutations.why: a declared form a ten-to-one majority of the code contradicts is refused, with both counts on the line

mutations.label: kind-mismatch
mutations.search: emit 1 kind-mismatch "$key" "$where" "kind '$kind' demands a '$expected_role' surface; the row declares ${surfaces_text:-none}"
mutations.why: a row's kind decides the grammatical role it must declare a surface in, so a value declaring only an operation is refused

mutations.label: unit-missing
mutations.search: emit 1 unit-missing "$key" "$where" "the attribute declares no unit, so its quantity has no scale"
mutations.why: an attribute carrying a physical quantity names its unit, so a bare number cannot be declared as a distance or a speed

mutations.label: bool-prefix
mutations.search: *) emit 1 bool-prefix "$key" "$where" "the boolean surface '$name' carries no prefix; accepted: $(paste -sd, "$tmp/boolprefixes.txt")" ;;
mutations.why: a declared boolean surface carries is/has/can, so a flag reads as a question rather than as a noun

mutations.label: unanchored
mutations.search: emit 1 unanchored "$key" "$where" "the row carries neither a case nor a rule anchor; looked in openspec/specs/**/spec.md and guidelines/*.md"
mutations.why: a row carrying neither a case nor a named rule is refused where it is written, so a definition no proof stands behind never enters the tree

mutations.label: twin-term
mutations.search: printf "1\ttwin-term\t%s\trow:%d\t%s and %s are both kind %s and exclude the same nothing\n", key[i], i, key[i], key[j], kind[i]
mutations.why: two rows of one kind that exclude neither each other nor anything else are one word written twice

mutations.label: lopsided-exclusion
mutations.search: printf "1\tlopsided-exclusion\t%s\trow:%d\t%s names %s and %s does not name %s\n", key[i], i, key[i], key[j], key[j], key[i]
mutations.why: an exclusion is mutual, so row A naming row B while B does not name A is refused naming both rows

mutations.label: unowned-term
mutations.search: emit 1 unowned-term "$key" "$where" "the row is declared global (a concept file) and homed '$home'; a global term's home kind is concept"
mutations.why: a global word's home kind is concept, so a feature word cannot be declared app-wide however many features use it

mutations.label: misplaced-term
mutations.search: emit 1 misplaced-term "$key" "${where2}" "the declared term is declared in a '$pkgkind' package ($pkgname); only concept and feature/<name> coin a term"
mutations.why: only a coining kind declares a term, so a declared word whose type sits in a port, platform or shell package is reported

mutations.label: bad-name
mutations.search: emit 1 bad-name "$key" "$where" "the declared type '$name' carries the suffix $suffix in kind '$home': $reason"
mutations.why: a vacuous suffix from the declared lexicon is refused in a coining kind, naming the type, the suffix and the lexicon's reason

mutations.label: undeclared-context
mutations.search: emit 1 undeclared-context "$key" "$where" "scope '$scope' is not a feature architecture/structure.tsv declares"
mutations.why: a row's scope names a feature the structure declaration carries, so the glossary cannot invent a context of its own
